chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the Quran was revealed in four quarters: a quarter is Permissible, and a quarter is Prohibitions, and a quarter is Sunnah and regulations, and a quarter is information of what was before you and news of what is to happen after you, and decisions of what (disputes there are) between you.
ai.seo_question: What are the four parts of the Quran according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines a comprehensive fourfold classification of the Quranic text, categorizing it into legal injunctions (halal/haram), normative practices and regulations (sunnah/ahkam), historical and eschatological narratives (khabar/naba'), and judicial resolutions (fasl). In Shia scholarship, this framework is often cited to demonstrate the Quran's self-sufficiency as a source of law and guidance, complementing the role of the Ahl al-Bayt in interpretation. The mention of 'sunnah' here refers to the Quranic precedents rather than the later technical definition of Prophetic tradition, highlighting the text's internal coherence.
